claims.text: The baseline is an as-cast, undoped MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration alloy with limited fracture toughness and ductility but a large magnetocaloric effect.
Approximately 0.5 at.% B should be introduced during arc-melting synthesis.
The arc melting should be performed under a protective atmosphere.
The alloy should receive a homogenization anneal at approximately 850 °C for a controlled duration.
The homogenization anneal will ensure uniform B distribution and prevent brittle B-rich secondary phases.
Low-level B will preferentially migrate to and segregate at grain boundaries in the MnNiSi-based alloy.
Grain-boundary B segregation will enhance intergranular cohesion.
Enhanced intergranular cohesion will inhibit crack initiation and propagation.
Inhibiting crack initiation and propagation will increase fracture toughness and ductility relative to the undoped baseline.
A B concentration near 0.5 at.% is low enough to preserve the magneto-active matrix.
Preserving the magneto-active matrix will conserve the alloy's magnetocaloric properties.
The B-doped alloy's magnetic entropy change will remain comparable to that of the undoped baseline.
The B-doped alloy's magneto-structural transition temperature will remain comparable to that of the undoped baseline.
The proposed benefits depend on maintaining B near 0.5 at.% and optimizing the homogenization process.
B-rich secondary phases caused by unsuitable composition or processing may degrade both mechanical and magnetocaloric properties.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that homogenization should ensure uniform B distribution, whereas the proposed mediator requires preferential B segregation at grain boundaries. These can only be reconciled if 'uniform' means macroscopically uniform grain-boundary coverage rather than chemically uniform distribution, but that distinction is not stated.
